items.stem: In the Keynesian cross model, equilibrium national income occurs where
items.answer: aggregate expenditure equals national output (income)
items.markingKey: AE = Y on the 45° line; equivalently injections = withdrawals.

items.stem: With the aid of a diagram, explain how equilibrium national income is determined in the Keynesian cross model.
items.answer: Diagram: AE on vertical axis, national income on horizontal; 45° line where AE = Y; AE = C + I + G + (X − M) slopes upwards with slope MPC (less MPM). Equilibrium Ye where AE cuts the 45° line. Below Ye, AE > Y so stocks fall and output rises; above Ye, AE < Y so output falls.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: axes and 45° line; 1 mark: AE line; 1 mark: equilibrium; 1 mark: adjustment [4]

items.stem: Explain why equilibrium national income is where withdrawals equal injections.
items.answer: Withdrawals (S, T, M) take spending out of the flow; injections (I, G, X) add to it. If J > W, spending exceeds output and income rises; if W > J, income falls; only when W = J is income stable.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: definitions; 1 mark: imbalance adjusts income; 1 mark: equality at equilibrium [3]

items.stem: In a closed economy with no government, C = 40 + 0.6Y and investment is $60 billion. Calculate equilibrium national income.
items.answer: $250 billion

items.stem: In Istrana (figures in $ billion): C = 50 + 0.9Y, I = 60, G = 150. Calculate equilibrium national income and the value of the multiplier.
items.answer: Y = $2600 billion; multiplier = 10.

items.stem: Extract: National income in Gorvania is $450 billion, while full-employment income is estimated at $500 billion. The marginal propensities to save, tax and import are 0.05, 0.2 and 0.25. The finance minister proposes a $25 billion infrastructure programme. (a) Calculate the multiplier. (b) With the aid of a diagram, explain the type of gap facing the economy.
items.answer: (a) 2 (b) Deflationary gap: AE cuts the 45° line below Yf; shortfall of AE at Yf.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the average and marginal propensity to consume.
items.answer: APC = total consumption/total income; MPC = change in consumption/change in income. With autonomous consumption, APC falls as income rises and exceeds MPC.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each; 1 mark relationship [3]

items.stem: In Marvona (figures in $ billion): C = 80 + 0.8Y, I = 60, G = 0, X = 80 and M = 0.05Y. Calculate equilibrium national income and the value of the multiplier. Government spending then rises by $20 billion. Calculate the new equilibrium and the change in consumption.
items.answer: Y = $880 billion; multiplier = 4. New Y = $960 billion (ΔY = 80); ΔC = 0.8 × 80 = 64.

items.stem: In an open economy with a government, the multiplier is equal to
items.answer: 1 / (MPS + MPT + MPM)
items.markingKey: k = 1/MPW where MPW = MPS + MPT + MPM.

items.stem: Explain the multiplier effect of an increase in investment.
items.answer: Extra investment raises incomes of workers and firms producing capital goods; they spend part of it (MPC), creating income for others, who spend part again; total income rises by a multiple of the initial injection, determined by the leakages (MPS, MPT, MPM).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: initial injection; 1 mark: rounds of spending; 1 mark: size depends on leakages [3]

items.stem: Explain why the multiplier may be smaller in practice than the simple formula suggests.
items.answer: High import propensity in open economies; progressive taxes; spare capacity may be lacking so prices rise; time lags; crowding out; confidence effects.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each reason [2]

items.stem: In Marvona, MPS = 0.1, MPT = 0.2 and MPM = 0.1. Calculate the value of the multiplier.

In Westaria, MPS = 0.1, MPT = 0.2 and MPM = 0.1. There is an increase in government spending of $25 billion. Calculate the multiplier and the final change in national income, and the resulting changes in saving, tax revenue and imports.
items.answer: k = 2.5; ΔY = $62.5 billion; ΔS = 6.25, ΔT = 12.5, ΔM = 6.25 (total withdrawals 25 = injection).
items.markingKey: k = 1/0.4 [1]; ΔY = 25 × 2.5 [1]; each withdrawal = propensity × ΔY [1]; total withdrawals equal the injection [1].

items.stem: In Westaria, MPS = 0.1, MPT = 0.1 and MPM = 0.05. There is an increase in investment of $20 billion. Calculate the multiplier and the final change in national income, and the resulting changes in saving, tax revenue and imports.
items.answer: k = 4; ΔY = $80 billion; ΔS = 8, ΔT = 8, ΔM = 4 (total withdrawals 20 = injection).
items.markingKey: k = 1/0.25 [1]; ΔY = 20 × 4 [1]; each withdrawal = propensity × ΔY [1]; total withdrawals equal the injection [1].

items.stem: Extract: National income in Zentara is $900 billion, while full-employment income is estimated at $1000 billion. The marginal propensities to save, tax and import are 0.1, 0.2 and 0.2. The finance minister proposes a $50 billion infrastructure programme. (a) Calculate the multiplier. (b) Assess whether the programme will achieve full employment.
items.answer: (a) 2 (b) Multiplier uncertain (MPM, confidence), time lags, crowding out, structural unemployment not addressed, inflation risk; borrowing costs.

items.stem: Extract: National income in Tarvia is $450 billion, while full-employment income is estimated at $500 billion. The marginal propensities to save, tax and import are 0.1, 0.15 and 0.25. The finance minister proposes a $25 billion infrastructure programme. (a) Show whether the programme would close the gap. (b) With the aid of a diagram, explain the type of gap facing the economy.
items.answer: (a) ΔY = 2 × 25 = 50: closes the gap exactly (in theory). (b) Deflationary gap: AE cuts the 45° line below Yf; shortfall of AE at Yf.

In Esteria, MPS = 0.1, MPT = 0.2 and MPM = 0.2. Calculate the value of the multiplier.

The government of Dravonia, a small open economy that imports most consumer goods, is planning a fiscal stimulus. Assess whether the multiplier makes fiscal policy a powerful tool for raising national income.
items.answer: Arguments for: Injections have multiplied effects on income; a well-targeted increase in G raises Y by k × ΔG. Arguments against / evaluation: High leakages (MPM) reduce k; crowding out; time lags; supply constraints; uncertainty about k. Conclusion: a supported judgement that depends on the conditions identified.
items.markingKey: Knowledge and analysis (about 60%): accurate theory, logical chains of reasoning and a relevant diagram described with axes, curves and shifts. Evaluation (about 40%): considers both sides, the assumptions and the context, and reaches a justified conclusion.

items.stem: A deflationary gap exists when
options: equilibrium income is above full employment
equilibrium national income is below the full-employment level of income
items.answer: equilibrium national income is below the full-employment level of income
items.markingKey: AE too low: spare capacity and demand-deficient unemployment.

items.stem: With the aid of a diagram, explain the difference between an inflationary gap and a deflationary gap.
items.answer: Keynesian cross with full-employment income Yf marked. Deflationary gap: AE cuts the 45° line below Yf; the vertical distance between the 45° line and AE at Yf is the shortfall in spending. Inflationary gap: AE cuts above Yf; the vertical excess of AE over the 45° line at Yf is the inflationary gap.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each correctly described gap; 1 mark vertical measurement at Yf [3]

items.stem: Explain how a government could close an inflationary gap.
items.answer: Reduce AE: cut government spending or raise taxes (contractionary fiscal policy) or raise interest rates; the fall in AE has a multiplied effect on income until it reaches Yf.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: policy; 1 mark: lowers AE with multiplier [2]

items.stem: Equilibrium national income in Halvoria is $600 billion and full-employment income is $560 billion. The multiplier is 2. Calculate the change in aggregate expenditure needed to reach full employment.
items.answer: $20 billion decrease
items.markingKey: Gap in AE = ΔY/k = 40/2 = 20.

items.stem: Equilibrium national income in Valdoria is $500 billion and full-employment income is $600 billion. The multiplier is 2. Identify the type of gap, calculate its size, and explain one fiscal policy to close it.
items.answer: Deflationary gap of $50 billion in AE (income gap 100). Raise G or cut taxes by enough to raise AE by this amount.
items.markingKey: Type [1]; AE gap = ΔY/k = 100/2 = 50 [2]; policy with multiplier [1].

items.stem: Unemployment in Korvia is high and firms have spare capacity. Explain what type of gap exists and how it could be closed.
items.answer: A deflationary gap: AE is below the level needed for full-employment output. Expansionary fiscal or monetary policy raises AE, and the multiplier raises income towards Yf.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: deflationary gap; 1 mark: policy and multiplier [2]

items.answer: (a) 2 (b) Multiplier uncertain (MPM, confidence), time lags, crowding out, structural unemployment not addressed, inflation risk; borrowing costs.

items.stem: The accelerator theory states that net investment depends on
options: the rate of change of national income (or sales)
items.answer: the rate of change of national income (or sales)
items.markingKey: Inet = v × ΔY, where v is the capital–output ratio.

items.stem: Explain how the interaction of the multiplier and accelerator can cause a boom to turn into a recession.
items.answer: Rising investment raises income via the multiplier; higher income growth raises investment via the accelerator. When growth slows (e.g. capacity limits), induced investment falls, which via the multiplier reduces income, further reducing investment, so the economy turns down.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: multiplier; 1 mark: accelerator; 1 mark: slowing growth reduces investment and income [3]

items.stem: Explain two limitations of the accelerator theory.
items.answer: Firms may have spare capacity; expectations matter; capital goods industries may be at capacity; the capital–output ratio is not fixed; investment also depends on interest rates and technology.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each identified, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: A firm’s capital–output ratio is 2. Year: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; Sales ($m): 100, 120, 150, 180, 190, 180. Calculate its net investment in year 5.

A firm has a capital–output ratio of 2 and replaces $30m of worn-out capital each year. Year: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; Sales ($m): 250, 260, 290, 320, 330, 330. Calculate net and gross investment in years 2 to 6 and explain what the results show about the accelerator.
items.answer: Net investment: 20, 60, 60, 20, 0; gross investment: 50, 90, 90, 50, 30 ($m). Investment rises and falls much more than sales, and falls once sales growth slows even before sales fall.
items.markingKey: Inet = 2 × ΔSales [2]; gross = net + 30 (not below zero) [1]; accelerator: investment depends on change in output, volatile [2].

items.stem: Extract: National income in Westaria is $450 billion, while full-employment income is estimated at $500 billion. The marginal propensities to save, tax and import are 0.05, 0.2 and 0.25. The finance minister proposes a $25 billion infrastructure programme. (a) Show whether the programme would close the gap. (b) Explain how the accelerator might add to the effect of the programme.
items.answer: (a) ΔY = 2 × 25 = 50: closes the gap exactly (in theory). (b) Rising income raises sales growth, inducing more investment, which further raises income.

items.stem: Sales of bus journeys in Merania are still rising but more slowly than last year. Explain why firms making bus journeys may cut investment.
items.answer: Under the accelerator, net investment depends on the change in output. Slower growth means a smaller increase in required capital, so net investment falls even though sales are still rising.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Inet = v × ΔY; 1 mark: slower growth lowers investment [2]

items.stem: A firm’s capital–output ratio is 4. Year: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; Sales ($m): 250, 260, 290, 310, 310, 300. Calculate its net investment in year 4.
Which is an injection into the circular flow of income?
items.answer: Exports
items.markingKey: Injections: I, G, X. Withdrawals: S, T, M.

items.stem: Firms in Dravonia become more optimistic and raise planned investment. Explain, using the Keynesian cross, the effect on equilibrium national income.
items.answer: Higher investment shifts the AE line upwards in parallel; at the old income AE > Y, stocks run down, so firms raise output until AE again equals Y at a higher income, by a multiple of the rise in investment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: AE shifts up; 1 mark: adjustment; 1 mark: multiplied rise [3]

items.stem: A larger marginal propensity to import will
options: have no effect on the multiplier
reduce the size of the multiplier
items.answer: reduce the size of the multiplier
items.markingKey: More leakage abroad in each round of spending.

items.stem: Kestria imports about half of the goods its consumers buy. Explain why its multiplier is likely to be small.
items.answer: A high MPM means a large share of each round of extra spending leaks abroad, raising the total marginal propensity to withdraw and so reducing k = 1/(MPS + MPT + MPM).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: high MPM leakage; 1 mark: smaller k [2]

items.stem: The government of Istrana raises income tax rates. Explain the effect on the size of the multiplier.
items.answer: A higher marginal tax rate (MPT) increases withdrawals in each round of spending, so the multiplier falls.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: higher MPT; 1 mark: smaller multiplier [2]
